# Native Rust 1.98.1 owned planning fixtures

These sixteen **fresh** positive observations were produced by successful ordinary
`plan_owned_migration` calls on original source
`8e1e5698437d9ea5c0d6ff2c0f29cf7af58d45a0`, ORM 0.50.2, under stock exact
Rust 1.98.1 (`48a229ceaefd4985c50990b14116b6d856af0985`), GNU x86_64
host/target without compiler wrappers, with the original root Cargo.lock.
They qualify `graphql-orm-owned-planning-8e1-rust1981-v1` for **new evidence**.
They were never generated from a replay verifier or copied/relabelled from the
twelve historical witnesses. Those [historical fixtures](../owned-planning-replay-8e1/README.md)
remain byte-identical, with their original 1.97.1 producer identity and recipe.

[Provenance and checksums](provenance.txt) bind the exact compiler/source/lock,
backend/image, [observational instrumentation](instrumentation.patch), each complete
compact witness and separate native plan Debug output. `.debug.txt` files retain
synthetic producer facts, not application metadata. The hook runs immediately
after the original live plan validation succeeds, retaining its actual source,
target, ownership/options and complete ordered steps/risks/reasons/SQL/hashes.
It adds no observation and changes no planner, renderer, Debug or hash algorithm.
Private serialization is observational only; expected native facts come from the
ordinary producer. Fixtures are not regenerated by conformance tests.

For each backend, both strict and managed-only options cover legitimate unowned
default/index metadata in a no-op, a nonempty addition containing U+3164, an
ordered compound One/Restrict FK and a table-create U+3164 default. Complete
wire/string/vector/null/empty distinctions are retained. Native capture and pure
replay compare all canonical bytes to these independently retained originals,
and all sixteen valid kind-last variants. Retained live capture bytes are decoded
and verified again after pool closure (and PostgreSQL container removal).
Original live observation counts and ordinary plan facts are compared as well.

Reproduce in an isolated checkout of the exact original source with its original
lock. The recorded patch retains an absolute, task-owned output directory: adjust
only that observational destination to a fresh private directory before applying.
Do not change engine algorithms or expected outputs. Then run only:

```sh
git apply --unidiff-zero /path/to/instrumentation.patch
cargo +1.98.1 test -p graphql-orm --offline --locked --no-default-features \
  --features sqlite --lib replay_fixture_positive_sqlite -- --nocapture
cargo +1.98.1 test -p graphql-orm --offline --locked --no-default-features \
  --features postgres --lib replay_fixture_positive_postgres -- --nocapture
```

SQLite uses owned memory databases. PostgreSQL uses only the existing labelled
Docker harness, proves `current_database()` before use and cleanup, closes pools,
then proves exact container ID and owner token before removal. The retained
positive producer logs (verbatim gzip-compressed `producer-*-output.txt.gz`)
record actual backend versions; both runs passed one
selected positive test and released resources.

## Paired producer comparison

`producer-comparison/` retains the earlier successful ordinary SQLite producer
comparison on exact 8e1, with the unchanged original lock. The complete input is
[orm-positive.rs](producer-comparison/orm-positive.rs); compiler metadata, complete
ordered output and commands/results are retained beside it. The temporary source
path in its command record has been released. Reproduction needs only a fresh
original archive and that additional example; no production source edit.

That case has an empty observed source and a `review_notes` target with U+3164:
source hash `cbf29ce484222325`, target hash `833642a1059a4851`, native owned plan
hash `1fdf860ccd8e7eca` on 1.97.1 and `d22edd67f4c4d8f5` on 1.98.1.
The values apply only to that retained case/backend. The new fixtures above have
their own actual source observations and backend-specific outputs; their hashes
are not assumed to equal the paired case. String Debug's native escape change
is intentionally preserved; no input restriction, normalization or historical
formatter emulator makes the recipes agree.

The standard-library source digest comparison and Unicode lookup-run descriptors
support the [per-recipe accounting review](../../../../../docs/reference/graphql-orm/owned-planning-replay-accounting.md).
They do not prove security/refusal properties. Wrong recipe/profile, malformed
input, resource exhaustion, sensitive disclosure, authority, concurrency and
cancellation remain inspection-only and runtime-unverified. No failed replay or
cross-compiler historical acceptance test is run. Positive conformance does not
authorize old receipt adoption, consumer changes, application or release.
